topic: Geometric Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Systems to Spaces

outline.topic: Geometric Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Systems to Spaces

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
sections.content: Introduce Ax=b as the intersection of hyperplanes. Visualize the system as constraints in space. Prerequisite: Basic understanding of vectors as coordinate points.
sections.example: A robot arm with two joints: each linear equation represents a constraint on an angle; their intersection is the specific pose of the arm.

sections.title: The Inverse Matrix: Unpacking the Transformation
sections.content: View the matrix A as a transformation grid. The inverse A⁻¹ is the 'undo' button. Explain that if a system is flattened (determinant 0), it cannot be undone.
sections.example: A photo-editing tool: Matrix A scales and rotates an image; A⁻¹ acts as the 'Reset' button that returns pixels to their original coordinates.

sections.title: Column Space: The 'Reachable' World
sections.content: Define Column Space as the span of the columns of A. Visually, it is the set of all possible output vectors b that the transformation can 'land on'.
sections.example: A cat moving in a 2D room: If the cat can only move along a specific diagonal plank, the column space is just that 1D line, regardless of how large the room is.

sections.title: Null Space: The 'Hidden' Kernel
sections.content: Define Null Space as the set of vectors x where Ax = 0. Visually, these are the directions that get 'squashed' into the origin.
sections.example: A security camera projection: Any movement of a person along the line of sight of the lens results in no change in the image (the projection is 0); that line of sight is the Null Space.

sections.title: Synthesizing the Big Picture
sections.content: Connect the concepts: If the Null Space contains only the zero vector, the transformation is invertible, and every point is reachable.
sections.example: A 3D printer: The 'Column Space' is the printable volume; the 'Null Space' represents design flaws where multiple distinct parts compress into the same coordinate, causing print failure.

storyboard.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
lecture_lines: Linear equations define constraints in our spatial world.
Imagine a robot arm constrained by these equations.
The intersection of these constraints identifies a pose.
animations: Display two vectors originating from the origin in 2D space. (Color: #FF5733)
Animate the vectors spanning a parallelogram to visualize the span. (Color: #33FF57)
Display the linear combination equation: c1*v1 + c2*v2 = b. (Color: #FFFF33)
Highlight the resulting vector b when c1 and c2 change. (Color: #33FFFF)
Rotate the view to show the geometric interpretation clearly. (Color: #FFFFFF)

storyboard.title: The Inverse Matrix: Unpacking the Transformation
lecture_lines: Matrices act as transformations on a grid.
The inverse matrix functions as an undo button.
Singular matrices flatten space, losing original information.
animations: Show a linear transformation map represented by a matrix A. (Color: #FF5733)
Visualize the inverse transformation mapping back to original. (Color: #33FF57)
Display the identity matrix I as the net effect. (Color: #FFFF33)

storyboard.title: Column Space: The 'Reachable' World
lecture_lines: Column space represents all reachable transformation outputs.
Visualize this as a span of vector columns.
The cat's reachable movement defines its column space.
animations: Show the column vectors as directions in space. (Color: #FF5733)
Visualize the span of columns as a 2D plane. (Color: #33FF57)
Indicate a vector b that lies within the plane. (Color: #FFFF33)

storyboard.title: Null Space: The 'Hidden' Kernel
lecture_lines: Null space contains vectors mapped to the origin.
These are directions squashed into zero space.
Think of the security camera's hidden line.
animations: Show a transformation mapping a line to the origin. (Color: #FF5733)
Label the kernel elements clearly near the origin. (Color: #33FF57)
Visualize the null space as a line or plane. (Color: #FFFF33)

storyboard.title: Synthesizing the Big Picture
lecture_lines: Invertibility requires a non-empty, unique space solution.
Null space collapsing points prevents perfect reconstruction.
Mapping these spaces defines our full system picture.
animations: Show the four fundamental subspaces interacting in a diagram. (Color: #FF5733)
Animate the orthogonal relationships between these subspaces. (Color: #33FF57)
Highlight the Rank-Nullity theorem relationship graphically. (Color: #FFFF33)
